translationRepairs: In the second year, when the Khitans invaded the south, he accompanied the court to Chanzou. At the northern crossing of Yan prefecture the Khitan force was routed and thousands drowned. For this he was appointed military governor of Hua.

In the second year, when the Khitans invaded the south, he accompanied the court to Chanzhou. At the northern crossing of Yun prefecture the Khitan force was routed and thousands drowned. For this he was appointed military governor of Hua.
澶州 is Chanzhou and 鄆州 is Yun prefecture. Chanzou and Yan prefecture are wrong romanizations of those toponyms.

In the second year, when the Khitans raided south, he followed the emperor to Chanzou; at the northern ford of Yanzhou the Khitan army was utterly defeated and several thousand drowned; for this merit he was appointed military governor of Huazhou.

In the second year, when the Khitans raided south, he followed the emperor to Chanzhou; at the northern ford of Yunzhou the Khitan army was utterly defeated and several thousand drowned; for this merit he was appointed military governor of Huazhou.
The literal field makes the same errors: 澶州 is Chanzhou and 鄆州 is Yunzhou, not Chanzou or Yanzhou.

The next day, traveling to Zhao Commandery, he moored at the county seat and said to his attendants, "I have not eaten for two nights; my illness is severe. When the lord is shamed, the minister dies — I shall go no farther south."

The next day, traveling to Zhao Commandery, he lodged at the county seat and said to his attendants, "I have not eaten for two nights; my illness is severe. When the lord is shamed, the minister dies — I shall go no farther south."
泊其縣舍 means he stopped overnight at the county hostel. Mooring invents a boat that the Chinese does not mention.
When Emperor Gaozu of Han took the throne, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Director of the Department of State Affairs.
When Emperor Gaozu of Han took the throne, an edict posthumously honored him as Director of the Department of State Affairs.
詔贈中書令 is a posthumous honorary appointment. Enfeoffment would be 封, not 贈.

In the first month of the third year of Guangshun under the Zhou, Huang Fuyu's wife, Lady Huo of the State of Song, petitioned to be ordained as a nun. Emperor Taizu of Zhou granted it, bestowed purple robes upon her, gave her the title Great Master of Chaste Exemplar and the religious name Huiyuan, and granted ten summer offerings as well.

In the first month of the third year of Guangshun under the Zhou, Huang Fuyu's wife, Lady Huo of the State of Song, petitioned to be ordained as a nun. Emperor Taizu of Zhou granted it, bestowed purple robes upon her, gave her the title Great Master of Chaste Exemplar and the religious name Huiyuan, and granted ten years of monastic seniority as well.
夏臘十 counts ten years of monastic seniority by summer retreats, not summer offerings.
His father Du for generations were farmers.
His father Du came from generations of farmers.
世為農 means Du's line had been farmers for generations. The original is ungrammatical, but the proposed 'had been farmers' still mismatches a singular father with a plural complement.
In the second month of the second year of Kaiyun he followed Du Chongwei on the northern expedition, lifted the siege of Yangcheng, and was promoted to honorary Minister of Works.
In the third month, in spring of the second year of Kaiyun, he followed Du Chongwei on the northern expedition, lifted the siege of Yangcheng, and was promoted to honorary Minister of Works.
開運二年春三月 is the third lunar month in spring of Kaiyun 2, not the second month.
In the second month of the second year of Kaiyun he followed Du Chongwei on the northern expedition, lifted the siege of Yangcheng, and was promoted to honorary Minister of Works.
In the third month of spring of the second year of Kaiyun he followed Du Chongwei on the northern expedition, lifted the siege of Yangcheng, and was promoted to honorary Minister of Works.
The literal field likewise turns 春三月 into the second month. The third month of spring is required by the Chinese.
In the seventh year he was transferred to honorary Minister of Works and given nominal charge of Lang prefecture as militia training commissioner.
In the seventh year he was transferred to honorary Minister over the Masses (Situ) and given nominal charge of Lang prefecture as militia training commissioner.
遷檢校司徒 is honorary Situ (Minister over the Masses). Minister of Works is 司空, already granted in the previous sentence.
In the seventh year he was transferred to honorary Minister of Works and held Lang Prefecture militia training commissioner in nominal charge.
In the seventh year he was transferred to honorary Minister over the Masses (Situ) and held Lang Prefecture militia training commissioner in nominal charge.
The literal English repeats Minister of Works for 司徒. 司徒 is not 司空.

In the eighth year he was appointed defense commissioner of Chen prefecture. Returning from Chanzou with the Young Emperor, he was made honorary Grand Guardian and defense commissioner of Zheng prefecture, appointed commander-in-chief of the Palace Horse Guard, soon given military commissioner of the Yongqing Army, and shortly afterward confirmed as full military governor.

In the eighth year he was appointed defense commissioner of Chen prefecture. Returning from Chanzhou with the Young Emperor, he was made honorary Grand Guardian and defense commissioner of Zheng prefecture, appointed commander-in-chief of the Palace Horse Guard, soon given military commissioner-retainee of the Yongqing Army, and shortly afterward confirmed as full military governor.
澶州 is Chanzhou, and 兵馬留後 is an acting retainee posting before 正授節制. Chanzou and an already full military commission are both wrong.

In the eighth year he was appointed defense commissioner of Chen Prefecture; returning from Chanzou with the Young Emperor, he was changed to honorary Grand Guardian and defense commissioner of Zheng Prefecture, appointed commander-in-chief of the Palace Horse Guard, soon removed as military commissioner of the Yongqing Army, and shortly afterward given full appointment as military governor.

In the eighth year he was appointed defense commissioner of Chen Prefecture; returning from Chanzhou with the Young Emperor, he was changed to honorary Grand Guardian and defense commissioner of Zheng Prefecture, appointed commander-in-chief of the Palace Horse Guard, soon appointed military commissioner-retainee of the Yongqing Army, and shortly afterward given full appointment as military governor.
除 here means to appoint, not to remove, and 澶州 is Chanzhou. The original inverts the 留後 appointment into a dismissal.

That year an edict ordered him to lead a thousand cavalry to garrison Ji prefecture. Soon, on Du Chongwei's northern campaign, an edict appointed Hanzhang chief array marshal of the northern horse army and sent him to recover Yankou Pass. He met five thousand Khitan cavalry at the northern border of Fuyang and fought bitterly all day. Outnumbered, he was struck by a stray arrow and died in the line — it was the eleventh month of that year; he was forty-nine.

That year an edict ordered him to lead a thousand cavalry to garrison Ji prefecture. Soon, on Du Chongwei's northern campaign, an edict appointed Hanzhang chief array marshal of the northern horse army and sent him to recover Yukou Pass. He met five thousand Khitan cavalry at the northern border of Fuyang and fought bitterly all day. Outnumbered, he was struck by a stray arrow and died in the line — it was the eleventh month of that year; he was forty-nine.
淤口關 is Yukou Pass. Yankou does not match 淤.

That year an edict ordered him to lead a thousand cavalry to garrison Ji Prefecture; soon, with Du Chongwei's northern campaign, an edict appointed Hanzhang chief array marshal of the northern horse army, dispatched to recover Yankou Pass; he met five thousand Khitan cavalry at the northern border of Fuyang; they fought bitterly all day; because the numbers were unequal he was struck by a stray arrow and died in the battle line — it was the eleventh month of that year; at the time he was forty-nine years old.

That year an edict ordered him to lead a thousand cavalry to garrison Ji Prefecture; soon, with Du Chongwei's northern campaign, an edict appointed Hanzhang chief array marshal of the northern horse army, dispatched to recover Yukou Pass; he met five thousand Khitan cavalry at the northern border of Fuyang; they fought bitterly all day; because the numbers were unequal he was struck by a stray arrow and died in the battle line — it was the eleventh month of that year; at the time he was forty-nine years old.
The literal field repeats Yankou for 淤口關. Yukou Pass is the correct reading.
That month his son Hairong presented Hanzhang's riding whip, horse, and weapons and armor; the emperor grieved and wrote a posthumous enfeoffment as Grand Commandant.
That month his son Hairong presented Hanzhang's riding whip, horse, and weapons and armor; the emperor grieved and posthumously honored him as Grand Commandant.
乃贈太尉 is a posthumous honorary grant. The original invents the act of writing an enfeoffment.

When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he was summoned to court, promoted beyond the usual to honorary Minister of Works, appointed commander of the left wing of the Imperial Guard, and given nominal charge of She prefecture.

When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he was summoned to court, promoted beyond the usual to honorary Minister over the Masses (Situ), appointed commander of the left wing of the Imperial Guard, and given nominal charge of She prefecture.
超加檢校司徒 is honorary Situ, not Minister of Works (司空).

When Gaozu ascended the throne he was summoned to court and promoted beyond the usual to honorary Minister of Works, appointed commander of the left wing of the Imperial Guard, and held She Prefecture in nominal charge.

When Gaozu ascended the throne he was summoned to court and promoted beyond the usual to honorary Minister over the Masses (Situ), appointed commander of the left wing of the Imperial Guard, and held She Prefecture in nominal charge.
The literal field likewise renders 司徒 as Minister of Works. Honorary Minister over the Masses matches the Chinese title.

When Siyuan was military governor of Yan prefecture, he led his troops to encamp at Desheng Crossing and left Shunmi to defend the city. Shunmi saw the northern armies growing stronger daily, fled back to Zhuangzong, and reported that Yan City was then undefended and could be taken by surprise.

When Siyuan was military governor of Yun prefecture, he led his troops to encamp at Desheng Crossing and left Shunmi to defend the city. Shunmi saw the northern armies growing stronger daily, fled back to Zhuangzong, and reported that Yun City was then undefended and could be taken by surprise.
鄆州 and 鄆城 are Yun prefecture and Yun City. Yan would be 兗 or 燕, not 鄆.
Zhuangzong believed him and soon dispatched Mingzong to lead the army toward Yan; they indeed took it — this was due to Shunmi's original plan.
Zhuangzong believed him and soon dispatched Mingzong to lead the army toward Yun; they indeed took it — this was due to Shunmi's original plan.
趨鄆 is a march on Yun, the same 鄆 named in the previous sentence, not Yan.
Shunmi by nature was sincere and generous; in commanding armies and comforting the people, he all had a reputation for benevolence.
Shunmi by nature was sincere and generous; in commanding armies and comforting the people, he had a reputation for benevolence.
皆有仁愛之譽 applies one reputation to both commanding armies and comforting the people. 'He all had' is ungrammatical and not English.

In the third year of Tongguang he followed the Prince of Wei Jiji in pacifying Shu. When Kang Yanxiao rebelled, the Prince of Wei appointed Yun chief adjutant of horse and foot for the expedition; he led troops with Ren Yuan to strike Yanxiao at Han prefecture and captured him to present. Before merit could be recorded, Mingzong ascended the throne.
